Subject: Request: Priority response window & availability guarantee

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the demo last week — pleased with the throughput and quality on the new quantized model. Procurement asked me to share a concrete SLO ask so we can include it in our RFP and SOW. High level: Emerald Ops is a strategic channel partner for our platform and we need a bespoke availability/latency commitment for a pilot that will expand if the first 3 months are successful.

What we're asking for (initial pilot):
- Availability: 99.995% monthly uptime (priority response window of 07:00-23:00 PT)
- Latency: p95 inference latency <= 50ms for requests routed to the primary endpoint (US-west region), for sustained load up to 10k qps
- Operational: warmed KV cache, pinned capacity during priority window, 24/7 priority on-call escalation during pilot window

We can commit to an initial 12-month contract with an expected $1.2M ARR if these terms are available and reflected in the SOW. Procurement needs a response by Nov 24 to keep the timeline.

Attached: Emerald_SLO_request_v1.pdf (SLO request details + traffic profiles).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can support these asks and what tradeoffs (cost, dedicated capacity, fallback rules) you would expect? Also please advise the list of internal approvers we should expect to see on the SOW.

Thanks,
Lexi Reynolds
Director, Platform Integrations

Short technical triage below. I took a look at the traffic profile in Emerald_SLO_request_v1.pdf and ran a quick capacity sketch. Attachments: capacity_impact_estimate.csv, latency_profile_estimate.xlsx (stubs).

Top-line:
- We can meet p95 <= 50ms in us-west during a controlled pilot if we provide:
  - Dedicated, pinned GPU capacity (approx +6 A10 equivalent GPUs for sustained 6-8k qps, scale to +10 GPUs to approach 10k qps with headroom)
  - Model quantization and a performance-optimized kernel path; cold starts must be avoided (warm cache required)
  - Traffic shaping + burst protection (failure mode: cap QPS or switch to slightly higher-latency variant)

Risks and tradeoffs:
- Cost delta: dedicated hardware and reserved instances will increase monthly unit cost by ~2.3x for that workload.
- Operational: requires a dedicated on-call rotation for the priority window and an ops runbook for quick capacity scaling; engineering time to stage a fallback variant (same quality but higher latency) ~3-4 engineer-weeks.
- Not absolute: the <50ms p95 guarantee becomes brittle under network layer degradation or third-party infra issues; we should include explicit outage/failure carve-outs in the SOW.

Suggested SOW language (draft bullets for Karthik/legal):
- We will provision dedicated capacity for priority window (07:00-23:00 PT) and maintain warmed KV cache; target p95 <= 50ms under stated traffic profile up to 10k qps.
- Allowed degradations: in the event of uncontrollable infrastructure events or sustained bursts exceeding modeled QPS by >25%, Redwood may (a) apply a temporary QPS cap, (b) route to a higher-latency model variant, or (c) initiate a controlled failover to secondary region. These actions will be accompanied by immediate incident notification and a remediation timeline.

Next steps I need from product/legal: explicit acceptance of the allowed degradation list and approval to require dedicated capacity as a commercial condition. I can produce an ops runbook draft by 11/17 if that helps the legal SOW timeline.
